introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO questions from Section C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions in all : question ONE (obligatoire, 31 marks), ONE question de la Section B et TWO de la Section C ». `regles_choix` porte le minimum exprimable par section (B : 1 sur 2 ; C : 2 sur 4) ; la question 1 (Section A) est obligatoire donc sans règle ; la consigne complète (4 questions en tout) est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : Q1 = 31 (7+4+7+6+3+4), Q2 à Q7 = 23 chacune (Q2 : 5+3+2+3+8+2 ; Q3 : 12+2+3+4+2 ; Q4 : 6+6+6+5 ; Q5 : 4+10+9 ; Q6 : 6+12+5 ; Q7 : 5+10+8), soit 100 points pour les 4 questions à traiter ; aucun écart avec les totaux imprimés en page de garde. Pour les blocs à plusieurs items (Q1 a, c, d), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des points imprimés des items.

Sujet scanné de 5 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 7, carte topographique de Kumba avec sa légende, fond de carte du Cameroun) ; filigranes et bandeaux gcerevision.com ignorés. Contrairement à d'ordinaires Paper 3, la carte de Kumba et le fond de carte du Cameroun SONT dans le PDF et ont été recadrés en PNG (la carte, pivotée de 90 degrés sur la page, a été remise à l'endroit). Le papier millimétré n'est pas fourni.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level. Aucune statistique précise n'est avancée sauf celles du tableau imprimé de la Q3 ; les ordres de grandeur géographiques (pluviométries, altitudes, dates de création d'organismes) sont donnés de façon prudente et sont à faire relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Q4 à Q7 : les corrigés de la Section C sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire géographique ; les ordres de grandeur (pluviométries de 1 500, 900 à 1 200, moins de 800 mm ; températures ; altitudes des plateaux et sommets), les dates approximatives (SODECOTON et SEMRY dans les années 1970, barrage de Lagdo au début des années 1980, centrales d'Édéa et de Song Loulou, réservoir de Lom Pangar dans les années 2010) et les exemples (parcs, festivals, jardins) sont donnés de façon prudente et à faire relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Q4 : le sujet porte « 4. (a) Briefly describe ... northwards from the Adamawa Plateau » ; les types de climat sont décrits par grandes zones (Adamawa, soudanien, sahélien) ; les valeurs numériques sont des ordres de grandeur.

questions.enonce_markdown: 4. (a) Briefly describe the characteristics of the climate types of Cameroon northwards from the Adamawa Plateau. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Going north from the Adamawa Plateau the climate changes from a cool, wet tropical type to a hot, dry Sahelian type, because the rain-bearing south-west monsoon weakens and the influence of the dry, dusty north-east harmattan increases with distance from the Atlantic and the equator.

**1. The Adamawa Plateau (about 7 degrees N), a modified Sudan (tropical) climate.**
- Altitude (roughly 1,000 m) moderates the heat: mean annual temperature about 22 degrees C, cooler nights, small annual range.
- Rainfall is high for the north, of the order of 1,500 mm a year, with one long rainy season (about April to October) and a short dry season.

**2. The Sudan type (the Benue basin and the northern plains, roughly 8 to 10 degrees N).**
- Hot, with mean temperatures near 27 to 28 degrees C and a larger annual range (the hottest months are March and April).
- Rainfall of the order of 900 to 1,200 mm falls in one rainy season of about five to six months (May to October); the long dry season (November to April) has the dry harmattan wind.

**3. The Sahelian type (the Far North, north of about 10 degrees N).**
- Very hot (maxima above 40 degrees C in the hot season) with a large annual and daily range.
- Rainfall is low (below about 800 mm in the Maroua area and less towards Lake Chad), erratic and concentrated in a short rainy season of three to four months (June to September); the dry season is long, hot and dusty, with a drying harmattan.

**Trend.** Northwards, annual rainfall and the length of the rainy season fall, temperature and the annual range rise and the dry season lengthens.

**Marking guide.** 2 marks for each climate type described with its temperature and rainfall characteristics (any three), or the equivalent in a clear comparison.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Show how these climatic characteristics have influenced:

(i) The types of agriculture carried out in this region. *(6 marks)*

(ii) The problems faced by farmers of the region. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Influence on the types of agriculture (6 marks).**
- *Adamawa Plateau: pastoralism and mixed farming.* The cool temperatures, plentiful rainfall and extensive grass cover, with fewer tsetse flies on the highlands than in the forest, favour extensive cattle rearing by the Fulani (Mbororo) with transhumance in the dry season; maize, groundnuts, tubers and vegetables are grown around the towns.
- *Benue basin and northern plains: cotton and cereals.* One rainy season of five to six months with a long dry season, which allows the harvest and drying of cotton, suits cotton (the main cash crop), groundnuts, sorghum, millet and maize. The dry season also suits the drying and storage of grain and the growing of dry-season sorghum on the clayey soils of the plains (the muskuwari).
- *Far North: drought-resistant crops and irrigation.* The short and unreliable rains restrict the main crops to millet and sorghum (drought-resistant cereals), with irrigation for rice and onions along the Logone and near the dams (for example the Maga area), and the rearing of cattle, sheep and goats on the sparse grass.
- *General effect:* a single crop season, so farming is seasonal; the rainfall gradient creates the zones of crops from south to north.

**(ii) Influence on the problems of farmers (6 marks).**
- *Drought and irregular rainfall* cause crop failure and poor yields, especially in the Far North; the rainy season may start late or end early.
- *Desertification and soil degradation:* the dry climate, overgrazing, bush fires and the cutting of wood for fuel expose the soil to wind and water erosion.
- *Floods and waterlogging* in the Logone floodplain when the rain is heavy, which destroy crops and cattle.
- *Water shortage in the long dry season* for livestock and for domestic use; rivers (mayos) dry up; pastures dry up and force the herds to move (transhumance), which causes conflicts between farmers and herders.
- *Pests and diseases* (locusts, grain-eating birds, insects) are favoured by the dry, hot conditions; the harmattan and heat damage stored produce.
- *Short growing season* means one crop a year, a long period of unemployment (the dry season) and rural poverty and migration.

**Marking guide.** In each of (i) and (ii), three developed points linked clearly to climate, 2 marks each.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) What interventions have been made by the government to overcome some of these problems? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Government intervention in the northern regions (any five well explained points, one mark each):
1. *Cotton development:* the state-backed company SODECOTON (created in the 1970s) supplies seeds, fertiliser and insecticide, gives credit and extension advice and buys the crop at a guaranteed price.
2. *Irrigation and dams:* the Maga dam and the irrigated rice schemes managed by SEMRY (set up in the early 1970s) around Yagoua and Maga, and the Lagdo dam on the Benue (early 1980s), which supports irrigation and produces hydroelectric power and regulates floods.
3. *Water supply:* boreholes, wells and small dams for people and livestock in the dry season.
4. *Fight against desertification:* tree planting and reforestation (including the Green Sahel operation), protection of the forest reserves and campaigns for improved wood stoves.
5. *Research and extension:* agricultural research (IRAD) on improved, early-maturing and drought-resistant seeds, with agricultural extension workers; veterinary posts and vaccination campaigns for cattle.
6. *Transport and marketing:* roads and the Ngaoundere railhead (the railway from Yaounde) to evacuate produce, and rural markets.
7. *Regional co-operation:* membership of the Lake Chad Basin Commission to manage the water of the basin.

**Marking guide.** One mark for each intervention explained with its effect, up to 5.
